links.outcome: Accuracy, robustness to misinformation, and hallucination for grounded (fine-tuned plus retrieval) LLM versus general LLMs
links.effect: AtlasGPT was fooled 14% of the time in adversarial misinformation testing versus 44% for GPT-4 and 68% for Gemini Advanced. Accuracy was 96% versus 88% and 93%. No hallucination was found.
links.quote: In adversarial testing, under which AtlasGPT was tasked with identifying medical misinformation, it was fooled 14% of the time, compared with 44% for GPT-4 and 68% for Gemini Advanced.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning a general LLM on subspecialty (neurosurgery) domain data
Neurosurgeon rating of LLM answer explanations for comprehensiveness, relevance and referencing

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks AtlasGPT (a fine-tuned and RAG-augmented LLM) against general LLMs on a neurosurgery exam bank, including adversarial misinformation prompts and clinician ratings of explanations, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or operational guardrail.
